article_title: Docker Compose 5.8.0 Adds Scheduled Jobs, Running Cron Triggers Inside the Docker Engine

content_preview.title: Docker Compose 5.8.0 Adds Scheduled Jobs, Running Cron Triggers Inside the Docker Engine
content_preview.summary: Compose v5.8.0 lets a top-level jobs: element run on a cron schedule that Docker Engine fires itself, finishing work v5.6.0 began six weeks earlier with manual-only jobs.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Docker Compose v5.8.0, released on November 17, 2026, adds scheduled jobs, letting a Compose file declare recurring work such as a nightly database backup and have Docker Engine itself run it on a cron schedule, according to the [release notes](https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/tag/v5.8.0). The notes describe the headline change plainly: "Scheduled jobs are now supported. A job is a one-shot unit of work declared in the top-level `jobs:` element of your Compose file, run on...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (five sections: Overview, What a job is, What's new in 5.8.0, Where this started, What we don't know). 668 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Technical detail (exit codes, cron fields, concurrency/missed_fires defaults, 5-run history cap) is precise and each specific traces to a cited source. Closing 'What we don't know' section is an honest, well-sourced absence statement rather than padding.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns) and read in full from the decompressed snapshots (sha256-verified against manifest.json before reading). source-0 (github.com/docker/compose releases/v5.8.0): confirmed verbatim quote 'Scheduled jobs are now supported. A job is a one-shot unit of work declared in the top-level jobs: element of your Compose file, run on demand or on a schedule.'; confirmed release date 17 Nov; confirmed Docker Engine 29.10+/org.mobyproject.jobs.v0/dockerd --extension-enable wording; confirmed up/create registration and down de-registration behavior; confirmed up refuses projects with scheduled jobs when the extension is off. source-1 (releases/v5.6.0): confirmed verbatim quote 'This release adds partial support for jobs: only manually-triggered jobs are supported for now, scheduled jobs are not yet available.'; confirmed release date 02 Oct. source-2 (docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/jobs/ — added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this review's commit per the policy's confirmation procedure; confirmed as Docker's own official docs site by its branding, Docker Inc. copyright, and docs.docker.com being linked from the already-allowlisted docker.com): confirmed verbatim quote 'the five most recent runs, rather than the Docker Engine default of 10 000'; confirmed exit-code table (0/container's own code/1/124/130) matches article exactly; confirmed five-field cron syntax, UTC default without timezone, concurrency: forbid default, missed_fires: one catch-up behavior, and job-registration immutability all as described in the article. source-3 (dev.to/alexgeorgiev17, independent developer, not Docker): confirmed both direct quotes verbatim — 'a job with a schedule trigger makes `up` refuse to run at all' and 'nothing starts, not even the unrelated `db` service' — appear in the snapshot exactly as quoted, correctly attributed to Alex Georgiev's independent test of v5.6.0. No hallucinated quotes, no misattribution found. Anthropic disclosure: not required - article does not mention Anthropic, Claude, or any Anthropic-operated product.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked against raw source text (exit codes, version numbers, extension name, cron field order, default concurrency/missed_fires values, 5-run retention figure, release dates) matches its cited source. The one derived figure — 'six weeks earlier' for the Oct 2 to Nov 17 gap — is actually ~6.6 weeks (46 days); this is loose but within normal journalistic rounding for a scene-setting summary clause, not a headline/lead figure, and not substantively misleading. Not treated as a correction-worthy error.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and technical throughout; no sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Docker Compose jobs or v5.6.0/v5.8.0 found in src/content/articles/2026-10 or 2026-11 (checked via grep -rli 'docker compose'). This is new coverage of a previously unreported-on feature.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurate News submission. All four sources read in full and verified word-for-word against the article's claims and quotes; the only automated finding (docs.docker.com missing from the allowlist) was a confirmable gap in the allowlist itself, not a content problem, and has been resolved by adding the host with a justification comment in this review's commit. No fabrications, no misattributions, no headline/lead claims unsupported by sources. Featured candidacy: 0 - routine, incremental vendor feature release (an experimental Compose feature for a developer-tool niche audience, not a broad-impact or industry-changing story).
